title: Disguised Cargo
description: A customs document upload claims to be a harmless PDF, but its actual content type on the wire says otherwise. Confirm the server checks the declared MIME type of the uploaded part, not just its filename extension.
successCondition: Book a shipment, then POST /api/booking/:id/documents with a file named "invoice.pdf" but whose multipart Content-Type is set to "application/x-msdownload" (or another disallowed type) returns 400 with error.code VALIDATION_ERROR naming the unsupported type, even though the filename itself looks like a PDF. Uploading the same bytes with mimetype correctly set to application/pdf instead succeeds with 201.
hints: Most HTTP client libraries let you set the multipart part's Content-Type independently of the filename — check your tool's multipart API for that override.
The allowed set is exactly application/pdf, image/jpeg, image/png — anything else, regardless of extension, should be rejected.
